summary.text: Antibiotic resistance is when bacteria change so that antibiotics no longer work to treat infections, and it is one part of the wider problem of antimicrobial resistance.
It arises through spontaneous mutation, horizontal gene transfer, and the pressure of antibiotic overuse in both medicine and agriculture.
The World Health Organization calls antimicrobial resistance one of the top global public health threats and warns of up to 10 million deaths a year by 2050 unless action is taken.

items.prompt: A doctor prescribes antibiotics for a condition they cannot treat. What wider risk builds up when this happens often?

options.label: Bacteria become easier to treat over time
The drugs lose their effect only in the patient
Resistance spreads faster through overprescribing
Only farm animals are affected, not people

items.explain: Overprescribing and inappropriate prescription of antibiotics have accelerated resistance, and many prescriptions are unnecessary.

items.prompt: Random mutations are rare. Why do they still matter so much in microbes that reproduce quickly?

options.label: Frequent, rapid reproduction raises the chance some gain a helpful mutation
Fast reproducers cannot repair any of their mutations
Mutations in fast reproducers are never rare at all
Fast reproducers pass on only the helpful mutations

items.explain: Although random mutations are rare, many microbes reproduce so often and so rapidly that some members are likely to acquire one that increases resistance.

items.prompt: A hospital says a patient has become resistant to a drug. Where does the resistance actually sit?

options.label: In the patient's body, which has learned to ignore the drug
In the microbe causing the infection, not the patient
In the drug, which has weakened over time on the shelf
In the hospital's hygiene, which has let the infection thrive

items.explain: Resistance is a property of the microbe, not of the person or other organism it infects.

items.prompt: Which step is aimed at reducing the spread of resistance?

options.label: Prescribing antibiotics for every cough as a precaution
Using more antibiotics on farms to stop infections
Stopping all new work on antibiotic research
Using narrow-spectrum antibiotics and better hygiene

items.explain: Preventive measures such as narrow-spectrum antibiotics and improved hygiene aim to reduce the spread of resistance.

items.prompt: A few bacteria in a large population happen to shrug off a drug, and the drug keeps being used. Over time, which kind becomes more common?

options.label: The easily defeated ones, since the drug favours them
Both kinds in equal numbers, as the drug has no effect
The naturally protected strains, since the rest are cleared
Neither kind, because the whole population dies off

items.explain: Strains with natural resistance become much more prevalent than the ones that are easily defeated by medication.

items.prompt: A newspaper says antibiotic resistance is a problem for the future. What did a WHO report say instead?

options.label: It is limited to a few hospitals in rich countries
It is happening now in every region of the world
It only affects people who are very old or very young
It will start only after the middle of this century

items.explain: The WHO report stated that this serious threat is no longer a prediction for the future but is happening right now in every region of the world.
